comments.body:
Read-only investigation complete. **Verdict: duplication.** But the evidence also rules out the naive remedy, and the size of the prize is smaller than it first appears.

## The evidence

At `924a93f21edf6c4066339feeb7fff2294244d917`, the graft-side net change from the shared merge-base touches **30,740 paths**. Of those, **30,730 already existed at the pre-graft tip `0e2a06ba03f5e32d25a8dac036be938177ade9a3` with the identical path and identical blob SHA.**

That is the decisive measurement. Identical content under different commit objects is what duplication looks like, and it is not what recovery looks like — recovered history would consist largely of events with no counterpart.

Concrete examples:
- `0016-37a3.../1788554319...-CREATE.json.retired` — blob `84edeaf...` on both sides
- `2a50-d624.../1788481683...-SNAPSHOT.json` — blob `21e691...` on both sides

## The grafted set

`git rev-list 924a93f2 ^0e2a06ba` yields 28,570 commits spanning `2026-08-29T18:49:43Z` to `2026-09-10T18:43:18Z`.

Authors: Joe Oakhart 17,396, Rebar Bot 9,135, `rebar-bridge[bot]` 2,039.

Message shapes are ordinary store traffic, not anything exotic: 4,157 `ticket: COMPACT`, 3,359 `CREATE`, 3,301 `COMMENT`, 2,846 `LINK`, 2,672 `FILE_IMPACT`, 2,263 push-retry merges, 2,092 `REVIEW_RESULT`, 1,936 `SIGNATURE`, 1,719 `EDIT`, 227 binding snapshots, 227 reconciler sync deliveries.

## The caveat that rules out the obvious fix

**Neither side is a superset of the other.** Divergence is small but real and runs in both directions:

- 2 comment files on `59a7-cb88-f2f9-4148` exist **only on the graft side**
- 37 files under `96f3-af59-ba26-4159` exist **only on the pre-graft side**
- 8 `.bridge_state/*` paths differ

So "drop the redundant copy" is not available. Dropping either side loses ticket events. Any reclamation has to be a **union** that preserves the 39 divergent files, not a deletion of one lineage. That is a materially harder operation than it sounded before this measurement, and it is the single most important constraint this investigation produced.

## Producer

GitHub Actions run `34514936676`, `Reconcile Bridge`, scheduled on `main` at `7842c4adc4ae5f572af303a14f985e1ea972c61c`, concluded successful. `last-pass.json` records pass `2026-09-10T18-38-02` completing at `18:43:11Z`.

Path: `run_bridge()` -> `_delivery_command()` -> `python -m rebar._store.push commit-and-push --message "chore: sync events from rebar reconciler [run 34514936676]"`.

Note that `924a93f2` is a **1-parent** commit, not an auto-reconcile merge. Both sides became reachable together later, at merge `56050e33e16dbdfe8e4262ecb86539060e00f6a8` on 2026-09-17.

**Unverified:** what originally created the parallel duplicate lineage. What is confirmed is that run `34514936676` *delivered* an already-existing duplicate side line — it did not create it. The root cause of the fork is still open, and until it is understood there is nothing preventing a recurrence. That gap deserves its own ticket.

## Reclaim estimate, and why the margin matters

The graft side accounts for **28,570 commit objects and 56,443 tree objects**. On a `cat-file` disk-size basis in a disposable blobless clone: ~5,109 KiB of commits plus ~122,984 KiB of trees, ~128,093 KiB before pack-delta effects — consistent with the observed ~101,186 KiB pack step.

Taking ~101,186 KiB as the realistic reclaim, against the measured all-heads blobless figure of 648,346 KiB and the CI limit of 563,200 KiB:

```
648,346 - 101,186 = 547,160 KiB
563,200 - 547,160 =  16,040 KiB of headroom
```

So this **would** bring the authorship gate back under its limit. But at the post-step growth rate of roughly 3.9 MiB/day, that headroom is consumed in about **four days**.

That is the honest read and it should govern any decision made on this ticket. Reclaiming the duplicate converts a hard block into roughly a week of breathing room. It is real relief and it is not a solution. Per ADR 0106 the only durable lever remains reducing reachable commit and tree objects at a scale this does not reach — so this finding does not substitute for that work, it buys time to do it.

**Unverified:** exact post-rewrite pack size. Establishing it would require a history-rewrite simulation with ref mutation, which is outside a read-only investigation and outside policy for the live tickets branch.

No writes were made to the tickets branch. No refs were created, moved, or deleted. No LLM gate operation was run.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

On 2026-09-10 the `tickets` branch gained 28,570 previously-unreachable commits in a single reconciler sync, moving a fresh blobless tickets-only pack from 496,938 KiB to 598,124 KiB in roughly 30 minutes. Baseline growth either side of the event is ~2.5 to ~3.9 MiB/day, so this was about 40 days of ordinary growth arriving at once.

## Evidence

Measured during the investigation on `stable-jobless-coot`:

```
0e2a06ba03f5e32d25a8dac036be938177ade9a3
  parents=92f8d2783e41c137d58ac91aff5ba46f6845a5c4
  date=2026-09-10 18:28:21 +0000
  subject=ticket: LINK 40d7-eca8-8726-4b14

924a93f21edf6c4066339feeb7fff2294244d917
  parents=540983c7e841f9c739c286d0292a3e28d7312f30
  date=2026-09-10 18:43:18 +0000
  subject=chore: sync events from rebar reconciler [run 34514936676]

is_below_ancestor_of_above=no
is_above_ancestor_of_tip=yes

unique commits introduced = 28570
oldest_new = b46a31cacd45c3d34ea8697a5eb47462f394599a  2026-08-29 18:49:43 +0000  ticket: EDIT 9d40-1db8-1bcc-4f91
newest_new = 924a93f21edf6c4066339feeb7fff2294244d917  2026-09-10 18:43:18 +0000
```

The later commit is not a descendant of the earlier one. A side history reaching back to 2026-08-29 became reachable from the branch tip in one step.

## Why this needs its own investigation

The two candidate readings have opposite implications and the Git evidence alone does not separate them:

- **Recovery.** The reconciler reattached genuinely valid ticket history that had become unreachable, in which case the branch was previously missing events and the real defect is whatever detached them.
- **Duplication.** The reconciler grafted a parallel line of already-represented events onto the tip, in which case the store now carries a duplicate history and will accumulate more on the next occurrence.

Under the first reading the event was a repair. Under the second it was corruption that a repair-shaped commit message conceals. Both produce the same reachability jump, so the distinction has to come from the reconciler's code path and its run log, not from the graph.

A merge commit observed nearby on 2026-09-09, `Merge origin/tickets (auto-reconcile during push retry)`, suggests the auto-reconcile-on-push-retry path as the place to start. That is a starting point, not a conclusion.

## Relationship to other work

This is the mechanism behind the step change that pushed the authorship gate's pack budget over its limit (`stable-jobless-coot`). Fixing that gate addresses where the measurement is taken; it does not address a reconciler that can add tens of thousands of commits in one sync. If the duplication reading is correct, ADR 0106's history reclamation work would also be reclaiming against a store that keeps re-growing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reconciler run `34514936676` is inspected and the code path that produced commit `924a93f21edf6c4066339feeb7fff2294244d917` is identified in source.
- [ ] The event is classified as recovery or duplication on evidence — specifically, whether the 28,570 commits carry events already represented on the branch before the sync.
- [ ] If duplication: the conditions that trigger it are reproduced in a test, and the reconciler no longer grafts a parallel history under those conditions.
- [ ] If recovery: the defect that made valid ticket history unreachable is identified and tracked, since silent event loss is the more serious of the two findings.
- [ ] Whether the condition has recurred since 2026-09-10 is established by measurement rather than assumed from the absence of reports.
compiled_state.title: Reconciler sync made 28,570 older commits reachable on tickets in one step: recovery or duplicated history is unestablished
